description.narrative: IFC is considering an equity investment of up to US$10 million in Alkemi Venture Fund II Scheme I (Alkemi II or the Fund), an India domiciled, early-stage venture capital fund exclusively focused on healthcare.

Preliminary Project Outcome assessment of: Strong-Very Strong. i). Stakeholders: Increased access to venture capital and value creation for health sector investees in India. The Fund will focus on investing in startups operating in healthtech (70%) and consumer wellness (30%) with a focus on healthtech delivery, diagnostics, med-tech, pharma, and prevention/wellness. Despite a rapidly growing demand for healthcare services in India, healthtech and Biotech, Medical Devices, and Diagnostics sectors represented only 5% and 1% of VC capital invested between 2019 and 2023 respectively If successful, IFC expects the Fund Manager to be able to address a clear financing gap for healthcare startups in the country. ii). Stakeholders: Increased access to services to customers/patient health outcomes: India has strong unmet demand for quality healthcare. Following the strategy of its previous fund, Fund II will invest in companies that deliver better access to quality healthcare services in India, with an option to invest 25% of capital outside India. Health outcomes will only be relevant when delivered in applicable industry verticals and/or emerging markets. Higher scores may be possible if the Fund Manager (i) limits its exposure to developed markets; or (ii) commits on a best-efforts basis to invest in female founded companies, targeting 25% with a female co-founder.
2. Preliminary Market Creation assessment of: Moderate-Strong. i). Competitiveness: Increasing competitiveness in India's VC investment in health. Despite an active VC market in India, less than 10% of the number of VC deals completed in India were focused on healthcare. By supporting Alkemi to scale, the Fund will help demonstrate viability of financing healthcare via the VC business model. IFC expects the fund's success will encourage other fund managers to raise funds with dedicated strategies to address healthcare challenges.
